newsitem.title: CANADA: Teck says Vasilkovskoye talks progressing.
newsitem.headline: Teck says Vasilkovskoye talks progressing.

text.p: Teck Corp said Wednesday that thorny talks on the Vasilkovskoye gold deposit in Kazakhstan were making progress while Placer Dome Inc reported it still hopes to recover US$35 million from the Kazakh government over its aborted attempt to develop the same lode.
"We're back in negotiations...We've made quite a bit of headway," Gary Jones, Teck vice president of business development, told a mining conference.

Teck won a tender in June to develop the Vasilkovskoye deposit with reserves of 14 million ounces but that plan broke down in August because of a dispute with the Kazakhstan government over an investment plan proposed by the government.
Kazakhstan later returned the right to Teck, which is working with First Dynasty Mines Ltd, in October.
Jones said Teck may proceed with the project if it can reach agreement on such issues as taxation, infrastructure and ownership rights on the deposit.
"We seem to be progressing," he said.
Vasilkovskoye has been dogged by controversy. Placer won rights to the project in 1995 after the government bypassed a tender organized by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
Placer later pulled out of the project, saying conditions of the agreement had not been met. Kazakhstan then organized a tender which resulted in the Teck deal.
The government was supposed to return a US$35 million deposit to Placer by July but failed to do so, Placer has said.
Placer chief executive John Willson said in an interview Tuesday that the company and Kazakh government are proceeding with plans to submit the dispute to arbitration in London.
But Placer is "far more optimistic" about recovering the money than it was a year ago, partly because Kazakhstan has acknowledged it owes the company the money, he said.
"They've conceded publicly...they owe us the money," but are hampered by a lack of funds, he said. "Various negotiations are going on."
The dispute could take months or years to resolve, he said.
